tldr: For the randomized-arm squared-Wasserstein contrast under known Laplace assay error, uniform root-\(n\) absolute risk and finite \(90\%\)-honest connected length are possible exactly when the exact-outcome validation fraction has positive lower limit. This resource characterization is proved over the entire compact \(H^1\) density parent, including support gaps, in the original marked experiment. Explicit data-only inverse-hinge projection and scalar Green alternatives also give a finite-sample polynomial bracket with numerical certificates and a remaining logarithmic gap. Both criteria have order \(n^{-1/2}\) on every fixed positive-fraction regime, and honest length is always at most twenty times minimax risk. The sharp finite-budget envelopes, their logarithmic factors and saturation, and the reverse uniform risk-to-length comparison remain unresolved. Known-Laplace whole-law theory is credited as a tool. The consumer is a prospective continuous-endpoint precision benchmark for the scalar used by waddR; its published observational application is not asserted to satisfy this experiment.
gap: Clean compact transport limits, fixed-linear-functional deconvolution, heterogeneous density recovery and clean transport intervals are established. Rousseau and Scricciolo \cite{rousseau2024wasserstein} also establish whole-law \(L^1\)-Wasserstein inversion, Laplace recovery and lower bounds. These results do not jointly give a sharp finite scalar risk and honest-width frontier for two unknown gap-containing true laws with a fixed exact/Laplace validation schedule; a whole-law lower bound does not transfer to the scalar target or to the marked likelihood.
